checks: A positive finite concave profile has finite one-sided endpoint limits and a positive lower bound near zero. Completion at a,b preserves concavity and makes K compact. Endpoint changes are volume-null and section-null: neither axial endpoint plane can coincide with a through-origin cut, and a nonempty intersection has codimension one inside that cut.

For w=T^{−T}u, the new unit normal is w/‖w‖, with the same cap orientation. The normal component of Tu along it is 1/‖w‖, so the section-area multiplier is |det T|‖w‖ and S u becomes |det T|T^{−T}(S u). The constant cut Jacobian transports the centroid linearly. Both sides of every cap fraction acquire |det T|.

Horizontal orthogonal transformations preserve the ball-normalized body and send each h to either ±‖h‖e₁. The half-weight pair preserves the contribution to the weighted cap mean and its vertical balance, and cancels its own horizontal balance. For h=0 the two copies coincide. For v=0 the pair is antipodal. The construction also works when the horizontal dimension is one.

The reflected normals lie in a fixed two-plane. The accepted constants give 4/9 in dimension two, 3/7 exactly in dimensions 3 through 9, and strictly above 2/5 from dimension 10. In d=2 the comparison to (d/(d+1))^d is equality. The accepted strict comparison for d≥3 transfers.

Checked original candidate 197c4420ab5b2852 §1 and its recorded source hash. The source gives the same affine/reflection construction and quotes 2/5 coarsely for d≥10. Accepted fact 03ec0bc313e02df5 explicitly provides the frozen sharper constant.

dependencies.mapping: For the ball-normalized and reflected body take E=span(e₁,e_z). Endpoint completion gives a compact full-dimensional convex body with the origin interior, hence with interior projected origin. Each new normal is unit and in E. Its full section centroid is zero, so the projected centroid is zero. The new weights are nonnegative, sum to one, and balance the section-area vectors. The theorem gives exactly the claimed c_d.
dependencies.status: Accepted at the reviewed repository snapshot.

overlap.comparison: Same weighted cap bound and constants. It applies directly when the original normals already lie in a plane, in particular in dimension two. For higher-rank original menus its planar-normal hypothesis is not supplied by the original statement. The ellipsoidal symmetry and reflection transport the records to a different menu satisfying that hypothesis.

readability: The affine section-area multiplier and the reflected pair bookkeeping are explicit.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The affine normalization and reflection give a two-plane menu with the same mean and all the hypotheses of the accepted projected stationary-section theorem.
